<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dcd39c49e53fd1543cc96763afbaedc5104ece5b` — the merge of head `3276f760ae7e127c8c0590a98db89ed7431caa2b` into base `e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dcd39c49e53fd1543cc96763afbaedc5104ece5b && git checkout dcd39c49e53fd1543cc96763afbaedc5104ece5b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb 3276f760ae7e127c8c0590a98db89ed7431caa2b && git checkout -B drift-repro e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb && git merge --no-ff 3276f760ae7e127c8c0590a98db89ed7431caa2b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3276f760ae7e127c8c0590a98db89ed7431caa2b`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the net diff `git diff 5dbeb7d7b7e1deb7a64bd3178d2faada69c3097c refs/review/pr-21100` (ref tip verified equal to the head above; merge-base with `origin/main` 8368f1c005 is 5dbeb7d7b7; two commits, 4 files, +242 / −5), card #21028 (body, triage grade 5923790135, claim 5924889103, os-dev-report 5926101196) and PR #21100's body and file list. Every source statement below is a `git show` / `git grep` by sha, never the working tree.

**(a) `packages/cli/src/commands/environments/create.ts`** — all three removals land and nothing else moves.
- The `clone-from` flag declaration, the `clone_from_environment_id: flags['clone-from']` request key and the `--clone-from` example line are gone (3 deletions). The only insertion is a six-line comment stating why the flag is absent; it promises no future capability.
- A caller passing `--clone-from` gets oclif's own refusal: the command declares no `static strict` (default strict, verified over `packages/cli/src/commands/environments/**` at the head), and `this.parse(EnvironmentsCreate)` is the first statement of `run()`, before `createApiClient`, so an unknown flag throws `Nonexistent flag: --clone-from` with no request made. No bespoke message exists anywhere in the diff. Cloning is not implemented. Direction 5923790135 is met on every item.
- Everything else is byte-identical: the flags `url`, `token`, `org`, `name`, `plan` (default `free`), `driver`, `artifact`, `activate` (allowNo), `format`; the body keys `organization_id`, `display_name`, `plan`, `driver`, conditional `metadata`; the activate path and the table/json/yaml output.

**(b) `packages/client/src/index.ts`** — the key is removed from the inline request type of `environments.create` (line 3006 at base) and the namespace docblock no longer lists it among what the CLI sends (line 2920); a four-line note is added beside the existing `template_id` note. Verified from source that the CLI's request travels through this type: `create.ts:104` calls `client.environments.create({...})`, and that method is the one `this.fetch(baseUrl + /api/v1/cloud/environments, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(req) })`, which the new pin records at. `git grep -niE "clone[-_]from|cloneFrom"` over the head, excluding `content/docs/releases` and every `CHANGELOG.md`, finds only the changeset, the new test, the new comment in `create.ts` and the new client note (plus one unrelated `clone-from-a-path` prose comment in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` about git clone); the four `client.environments.create` calls in `client.environments-namespace.test.ts` do not name the key (zero hits for `clone` in that file); no exported type alias names the request shape. Grading: removing an optional member from a published request type shrinks the set of accepted call shapes (an object literal that still passes the key fails the excess-property check), so it is a narrowing, BREAKING, carried as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` until GA; the stock reads the same way, e.g. `.changeset/20822-driver-sql-turso-copies.md` and `20646-migrations-entry-split.md`). Correct.

**(c) The pin `create-clone-from.test.ts` (4 cases)** drives the real command through `EnvironmentsCreate.run(argv, { root: CLI_ROOT })` with `createApiClient` mocked to hand back a real `ObjectStackClient` whose `fetch` option (declared at `index.ts:213`) records every request and answers the create route's envelope. Assertions are at the wire. Pre-fix reasoning from the pristine `create.ts` of 5dbeb7d7b7: the control is green there too (the flag unset gives `undefined`, which `JSON.stringify` drops, so the key set is already exactly `display_name`, `organization_id`, `plan`), both refusal cases are red (flag accepted, exit 0, one request), and the declared-flag/examples case is red; 3 of 4 red matches the dev's numbers. Ablation leg 1 (flag re-added) reproduces that. Leg 2 planting the key with a constant is the right ablation for the key half: a literal restore of `flags['clone-from']` with the flag undeclared is `undefined` and invisible on the wire, so the constant is what proves the key-set equality has teeth; it is not a proof of the original coupled shape, but the pristine-tree and leg-1 runs are. The examples case carries a non-vacuity control (`--org`, `--artifact` must be spelled). The 60s budgets are wall-clock only, mirroring the existing `delete-arms-agree.test.ts` (present at the head). The file spawns nothing and boots no kernel, so it falls in the cli `unit` tier by the derived partition; `Test Core` is green on this head. Minor: the refusal exit is pinned as non-zero, not as the exact `2` the changeset states (that number rests on the dev's real-entry run).

**(d) Changeset `.changeset/21028-environments-create-clone-from-removed.md`** — `@objectstack/cli: minor`, `@objectstack/client: minor`, a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (also on the PR body), and exactly one adr-0087 HTML-comment marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The arm is the only honest one on the facts: `registered` would put a non-metadata row in a ledger `objectstack migrate meta` cannot act on; both packages publish (not `unpublished`); nothing pre-dates the base (not `already-registered`); `runtime-interface-only` has no exported interface symbol here and inherits the prescription refusal; `type-surface-only` fails its predicate 4, since the request type was concrete at base and lost a member rather than moving off `any`. ADR-0087 D8 says in terms that `no-migration-prescription` "cannot tell a prescription for a metadata upgrader from a prescription for a source-code consumer, and only the first is the ledger's business", and the shipped stock carries the same class on the same arm (cli CHANGELOG: a command-name retirement, two `--json` output-key renames, one entry that states the residual outright). On the FROM/TO question: AGENTS.md asks that the body "state the FROM → TO mapping and the one-line fix" and mandates no syntax; a removal has no TO name, which the gate's own #18745 section says is why the only thing to write is an instruction, and the body states it ("Remove `--clone-from` with its id from the command, or `clone_from_environment_id` from the object you pass to `client.environments.create`"). Read against the detector by hand: no FROM/TO label, no arrow, no table, so `findMigrationPrescription` returns null; the gate passed in CI. Accuracy: the before/after behaviour, the refusal text, the unchanged create-without-flag body and the unaffected flags/fields all match the diff and the pin. Two precision notes, neither a false claim: "a call that passes it fails to compile" holds for object-literal callers (the common case); a caller passing a pre-built wider object still compiles and the key is still dropped server-side, so no runtime difference either way. "Starter content is still installed afterwards from the App Marketplace (`os package install`)" repeats the existing `--template` docblocks; `packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts` exists at the head, and nothing beyond its existence was measured here.

**Checks on the head** (`.../commits/3276f760ae.../check-runs?per_page=100`, 34 runs, every one `completed`, collapsed latest-per-name, so converged): the seven required contexts are all `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and all six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (and all three shards), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also `success`: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, all four `Type Check ·` jobs, the three PR-hygiene guards, `Auto Label`, `filter`. `skipped`: `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. No failure, no in-progress. **Merge-tree:** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/review/pr-21100` against `origin/main` 8368f1c005 wrote tree 62b2b15e7d with no conflicted path, exit 0; none of the four paths is `merge=os-regen`-routed (checked against `.gitattributes` at `origin/main`), so the local answer is GitHub's answer for this diff, and GitHub reports `mergeable_state: clean`. `origin/main` has not moved under either touched file since the merge-base and still carries the old lines, with no new consumer of the key.

### ② Semver level

Right for both packages. `@objectstack/cli`: a flag the command accepted is refused, a narrowing of the accepted argv; nothing newly accepted. `@objectstack/client`: an optional request-type member is removed, a narrowing of the accepted call shapes; nothing widens. Both carry `minor` with the BREAKING banner under the launch-window convention, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and one `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition that is the only honest arm available. The `patch` reading ("runtime unchanged") would hide a compile break ADR-0087's #13080 addendum says must keep its token.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 (leg-2 constant):** accepted; the reason given is correct and the file header states the same limitation, so the pin's reader is told what the control does and does not prove.
- **Deviation 2 (refused first leg-1 attempt):** accepted; nothing ran, restore proven by blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`, leg redone.
- **Deviation 3 (FROM/TO in prose):** accepted on substance, flagged on form. The arm is honest and the phrasing is within AGENTS.md's letter, but the shape was chosen against the detector and that is disclosed only in the report and PR body; the marker's own `why` does not say that the body carries a source-author prescription the ledger does not serve (ADR-0087 D8), which is what the stock's most careful entry of this class states in the marker so the next author reads a positive argument rather than a detector miss. Not a defect in this landing; worth carrying into the marker if the changeset is touched again.
- **Deviation 4 (`add_repo` read of objectui):** proper. Post-Task step 4 mandates the pinned-sibling grep at `.objectui-sha` before merging a removal; the dev used read access, a shallow fetch into scratch, no write and no sibling file touched. The result (zero hits, positive control found `environments.*` calls in `packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/provisionEnvironment.ts`) is outside this review's inputs and `Console Pin Gate` is `skipped` on this head, so the sibling clearance rests on the dev's reading alone. Given what is removed is an optional member nothing in that reading names, this is a disclosure, not a blocker.
- **Deviation 5 (`size/m` label):** accepted; the label is `Auto Label`'s, the dev wrote none, consistent with the rule that state you did not set belongs to another actor.
- **Out-of-scope note, "carrier: none":** right. Per `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` the carrier is the PR or person who will touch it; none is answerable, no evidence shows any other key is dropped, and Prime Directive #10 files a card only on named evidence, so Acceptance notes is the correct home. Nothing in this diff depends on the answer.
- **Docs:** zero hits for `--clone-from`, `clone-from`, `clone_from_environment_id` or `cloneFrom` at the head across `content/docs/**`, `docs/**`, `skills/**` and `apps/docs/**`; `content/docs/releases/**` and every `CHANGELOG.md` are untouched and carry no mention either. No doc owes an update.
- **Governance and landing shape:** no governed path in the file list (`.changeset/**`, `packages/cli/src/**`, `packages/client/src/**` only); head repo equals base repo; 247 changed lines; PR is draft and unarmed; commit trailers carry the model-free pair; no model identifier in the diff, the PR or the changeset. Not a Tier S surface, so this record is a contract-tier review on request, not a landing precondition.
